one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company event falls inside the window. 2026-11-01 is a Sunday, so the scored close is Friday 2026-10-30. Q3 results most likely come on Wednesday 2026-11-04: Materion has reported Q3 33 days after quarter end every year from 2022 to 2025, Q3 2026 ends Oct 2, and MarketBeat estimates Nov 4 [18,19]. My round-1 Oct-29 date was a data-provider placeholder [3], so there is no earnings jump in the window. What remains is short-horizon behaviour after an unexplained +16% two-day spike to all-time highs on Oct 1-2. No 8-K was filed, and the Jefferies initiation came a month earlier [19]. Short interest is rising: 594.7k shares (2.89% of float) vs 497.0k a month earlier, +20% [16]. That spike argues for mild reversal risk, while momentum argues the other way. I tilt the median only slightly down, to ~$309 (-1%). Sigma is ~15.5% over the month: annual vol 59%/3.5 = 16.9%, less the share of realized vol that came from the Aug 5 +30.8% earnings day [19]. The result is a lognormal ladder close to symmetric around spot.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods, 45/45/10. P/E: 2028E EPS $9.78 x 26x NTM = $254. EV/EBITDA: NTM EBITDA as of Oct-2027 of $340M x 19x, minus ~$330M net debt, over 21.1M diluted shares = $290. FCF yield: 2027E FCF of $170M ($8.06/share) at a 3.5% yield = $230. Blended fair value is ~$268, 14% below $312. Both multiples sit inside the 10-peer range: P/E is a modest premium to the 24.3x median and EV/EBITDA is in line with the ~18.8x median.

inputs_detail.derivation: The Q2 8-K set the guide; the supervisor's check of the Q1 8-K shows Q1 only reaffirmed $6.00-6.50.

Consensus is $8.43 (stockanalysis) to $8.48 (MarketBeat). I use $8.50, about at consensus, and drop round-1's upward nudge because the H2 guide implies ~$1.92/qtr against $1.89 Q3 consensus, an in-line bar [19].

Consensus FY27 growth is +20% [17] and peers' median next-year EPS growth is ~24% [peer forecasts]. I haircut to 15% for 54% semis exposure (cyclical), margin normalisation from 32% EM EBITDA, and Q2 one-offs [1,2].

The 10-peer median forward P/E is 24.3x (range 14.5-39.7). The A&D alloy subset (CRS, ATI, HWM, HXL) is ~33x and the semis-materials subset (ENTG, ESI, MKSI, UCTT, PLAB) is ~18x. By value-added sales Materion is mostly semis/industrial with ~20% A&D, so a mix-weighted multiple is ~24-25x. I allow a ~1.5x premium for the persistent, structural sole-source integrated US beryllium position, backed by Materion's own 5-year median P/E of 28.8x [10]. See comps_summary.

methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA as of Oct-2027 $340M x 19x = EV $6.46B; less net debt ~$0.33B; / 21.1M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: The FY2026 run-rate is ~$265M (Q2 $71.8M x ~3.7). I grow it ~13%/yr in line with consensus revenue growth of +9% [17] plus modest operating leverage. I trim $5M from round 1 for Q2 one-offs that management said may not repeat [2].

The 10-peer median derived forward EV/EBITDA is ~18.8x (range 4.2-30.4). 19x is at the median, with no premium. Materion's own is ~31x on stockanalysis TTM EBITDA and ~26x on adjusted FY26 EBITDA [16,1].

inputs_detail.derivation: $340M EBITDA less ~$100M capex, ~$45M cash tax, ~$25M interest; working capital roughly neutral. Unproven given 2022-2025 FCF history, hence 10% weight.
In the range of quality specialty-materials peers trading at ~25-35x earnings [22,30]. This leg is a check, added because the supervisor flagged FCF as only now inflecting.

bear.story: Semis/AI or space orders pause after 2026, and EM margins normalise from 32%. 2027 EPS comes in ~$7.5 and the multiple falls to ~22x, the low end of the A&D/semis-materials peer mix. The momentum and theme flow that drove the unexplained Oct 1-2 spike reverses.

base.story: 2027 EPS lands at the ~$8.45 consensus and the 2028 path is ~$9.7. The multiple converges toward a mix-weighted peer level (~26-29x NTM vs ~37x today), so the price drifts modestly below spot.

bull.story: Defense beryllium capacity, space and AI-chip demand push 2027 EPS above $9.5 and the 2028 path to ~$12. The multiple holds near the A&D alloy peers (~33-37x), and the stock graduates from small-cap indices, bringing new index demand.

thesis_break_reason: $190 is where the stock sat before the Q2 beat ($189.34 on 2026-07-29) [19], ~22x FY2027 consensus, below the 24.3x peer median. Trading there would mean the 2026 re-rating has fully unwound and the stock is priced below its peer group. That most likely comes from a guidance cut or a reversal in backlog or semis orders, not ordinary volatility. Note that the stock fell 36% in July 2026 with no earnings news [19], so drawdowns of this size can happen without a fundamental cause. I would want a fundamental trigger to confirm the break.

reasoning: Supervisor corrections adopted: guidance was raised once, not twice; Q3 most likely reports Nov 4, outside the 1-month window; the 'Q2 sales beat ~25%' claim is dropped as unsourced; the SpaceX theme stays out of the numbers [19]. The fundamentals are unchanged: Q2 adj EPS $1.90, FY26 guide $6.80-7.20, backlog +30% [1]. FY27 consensus is $8.43-8.48 [17,18]. The new work is a 10-peer comps set (stockanalysis, 2026-10-02) [22-41]. Its median forward P/E is 24.3x and its median derived forward EV/EBITDA ~18.8x, against MTRN at 39.4x and ~31x [16]. Peers' next-year EPS growth has a median of ~+24%, vs MTRN's +20% [17]. MTRN does not out-grow its peers, so I cut my P/E from 28x to 26x, a small premium argued only on the beryllium moat and its own 5-year median. I keep EV/EBITDA at 19x, the peer median, and add a 10% FCF-yield check. Fair value falls from $286 to $268. In-lane positioning evidence: short interest rose 20% m/m to 2.89% of float [16]; Russell moved MTRN from value to dynamic/growth indices in June [20]; its largest ETF holder is the S&P SmallCap 600 fund IJR [21], with a market cap now large for that index. That suggests momentum/growth-style ownership, which can unwind fast (the July -36% drawdown had no earnings news [19]). I set the 12-month median ~$288 (-8%). It sits above fair value because estimate revisions and momentum tend to persist, but below spot because the multiple is far above peers. Dispersion is lognormal sigma ~0.47 with slightly fat tails. The scenario mean is ~$294. Research was limited: Twelve Data statistics needs a paid plan, X/Reddit were unreachable, and etfbeacon returned 429. No option data was used.

comps_summary.why_not_more: Ten is the number of genuine listed comparables I could find. Materion has no pure-play listed peer: the other beryllium producers are private, state-owned or non-US (e.g. Kazakhstan's Ulba). Rogers Corp returned no data. Larger diversified names (Amphenol, Applied Materials) are not comparable businesses. The set spans the A&D-alloy and semis-materials businesses that make up Materion's mix.
comps_summary.mtrn_current: fwd P/E 39.4x [16]; ~31x derived forward EV/EBITDA (EV $6.99B / TTM EBITDA $205.5M x 1.092) [16,17]; FY27 EPS growth +20.1%, revenue +9.2% [17]
comps_summary.mtrn_in_fair_value: P/E 26x NTM at horizon: a 7% premium to the 24.3x median, inside the range, between the semis-materials subset (~18x) and the A&D-alloy subset (~33x). EV/EBITDA 19x: at the ~18.8x median, inside the range.
comps_summary.justification: MTRN's current 39.4x forward P/E is at the top of the peer range, and its growth does not earn that. Next-year EPS growth of +20% and revenue growth of +9% are below the peer medians of +24% and +12% [17, peer forecasts]. Its EBITDA margin on net sales is only ~10% because of precious-metal pass-through, vs ~25-30% at ENTG/CRS. EPS was flat over 2022-2025, FCF has only just inflected, and 54% of net sales are semis-cycle exposed, so the business is no less cyclical than peers. None of those supports a persistent premium. The one structural factor is Materion's position as the only integrated US beryllium producer. That moat has lasted for decades and underpins its 5-year median P/E of 28.8x [10]. On that basis I allow a small premium on P/E (26x vs 24.3x median, roughly a mix-weighted 24-25x plus ~1.5x) and none on EV/EBITDA (19x = median). Both sit inside the peer range. The balance sheet (net debt ~1.6x EBITDA) is neither a reason for a premium nor for a discount. Sell-side Buy ratings were not used as justification. Caveats: forward EV/EBITDA is derived (TTM EBITDA grown at next-year revenue growth); fiscal years differ for CRS (June) and PLAB (October); UCTT and KALU are distorted by recovering or falling earnings.
